Your atmosphere, in motion.
Choose a weather front, tune its parameters, and watch the landscape respond. This is a visual weather sandbox, not a forecasting model.

Rain, snow, and dust can be combined. Preset transitions do not erase accumulated surface wetness or snow. Audio is synthesized locally and starts only after you enable it. Sky flashes are disabled by default.
One world. One weather engine.
The source bundle includes an engine-only ES module. Pass in Worldworks’ Three.js namespace, scene, and camera, then update it from the existing loop. It does not create a renderer or a second animation loop.
const weather = new WeatherSystem({ THREE, scene, camera,
  groundHeight: (x, z) => terrain.sampleHeight(x, z)
});
weather.setPreset('storm');

// In your existing loop:
weather.update(deltaSeconds);
// On terrain edits:
weather.rebuildGroundField();
The HTML exposes window.Weatherworks for local scripting. Export/import stores versioned JSON settings and surface state. No uploads are made. The demo tries Three.js r180 online; the built-in WebGL2 renderer uses the same scene and shaders when offline. Weatherworks is not yet patched into your Worldworks file.
Cloud lighting, fog, water highlights, and surface accumulation are artistic approximations. Height-field precipitation occlusion is not full mesh collision or indoor physics. Host materials need to consume the engine’s wind, wetness, snow, and lighting uniforms to react.
